case: The training programme needs a cluster design, which I found hardest in lab 2.3, so I want to do it once more.

flaws: The redesigned form logged no applicant on an old mobile browser, so the arms no longer hold comparable applicants and every comparison leans towards the redesign.
Applicants were randomised but page views were analysed; counted per applicant, the difference in validation errors is not significant.
The pre-registered primary metric, completion, shows no clear effect; the headline metric was chosen after the data were seen.
The test was stopped on day 8 of 28 at a significant daily look, a rule that declares a win in a large share of tests with no effect.
Fourteen metrics and several subgroups were examined and the best were reported, so some apparent gain is expected by chance alone.
Eight days cover one weekend and no month-end, and first reactions to a new form may fade.
One form was tested for eight days; nothing supports replacing all forms or the figure of 9,000 completed applications a year.
memo.next_step: Fix the old-browser fault, then run the test again for the full 28 days as pre-registered, with one analysis at the end, completion as the primary metric, applicants as the unit of analysis and a sample ratio check before the result is read.
memo.supported_decision: The evidence does not support rolling out the redesign. It supports one finding the write-up dismissed: the redesigned form does not work on old mobile browsers, which must be fixed before any further test. On completion, the pre-registered metric, the test shows no reliable difference.
